import pytest, threading, urllib.request, json, os, sqlite3
from app import Handler, DB_PATH, init_db
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def setup_db():
    if os.path.exists(DB_PATH): os.remove(DB_PATH)
    init_db()

@pytest.fixture
def server():
    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
    port = httpd.server_port
    thread = threading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever)
    thread.daemon = True
    thread.start()
    yield port
    httpd.shutdown()
    httpd.server_close()

def test_flow(server):
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}/entries", data=json.dumps({"name": "A", "score": 10}).encode(), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    urllib.request.urlopen(req)
    res = urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base}/").read().decode()
    assert "A" in res
    assert "10" in res

def test_invalid_score(server):
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}/entries", data=json.dumps({"name": "B", "score": 2.9}).encode(), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        urllib.request.urlopen(req)
    assert e.value.code == 400

def test_duplicate(server):
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server}"
    req1 = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}/entries", data=json.dumps({"name": "C", "score": 5}).encode(), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    urllib.request.urlopen(req1)
    req2 = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}/entries", data=json.dumps({"name": "C", "score": 6}).encode(), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        urllib.request.urlopen(req2)
    assert e.value.code == 409
